brief.greeting: Good morning. The AI press released more paperwork than models, and the kernel finally got a license makeover.

stories.headline: OpenAI rolls out layered guard against distillation
stories.body: **Layered defense deployed:** OpenAI outlines training safeguards, detection mechanisms, and enforcement steps to stop adversarial distillation attacks.
stories.why: Engineers get concrete knobs to harden models against stealthy extraction.

stories.headline: Anthropic closes IPO, underwriters buy extra shares
stories.body: **IPO wraps up:** Anthropic announced its public offering is complete and underwriters exercised their option for additional stock.
stories.why: More capital means faster AI tooling updates you’ll end up using.

stories.headline: LLVM relicensing hits 99.5% Apache‑2.0
stories.body: **License overhaul finished:** Over 99.5% of LLVM’s codebase now sits under Apache‑2.0 with the LLVM exception after an eight‑year effort.
stories.why: Simplifies mixing LLVM into proprietary and open‑source projects.

quick_hits.text: **Security update:** LWN reports dozens of package patches across major Linux distros on Friday.

**Hackaday hack:** Convert HDMI output to a CSI camera interface for easy video digitization.

highlights.title: Combatting adversarial distillation
highlights.summary: OpenAI outlines a layered defense against adversarial distillation, integrating training safeguards, detection mechanisms, and enforcement steps.
highlights.detail: The approach aims to prevent extraction of model capabilities by combining multiple protective stages. It builds on prior adversarial robustness work but adds enforcement to limit misuse. No specific performance metrics are provided.

highlights.title: Anthropic announces closing of initial public offering, including full exercise of underwriters’ option to purchase additional shares, and closing of concurrent private placement
highlights.summary: Anthropic announced the closing of its IPO and full exercise of underwriters’ option for additional shares.
highlights.detail: The filing confirms the company completed its public offering and private placement simultaneously. Financial terms were not disclosed in the brief announcement.

highlights.title: Security updates for Friday
highlights.summary: LWN reported security updates for multiple Linux distributions covering dozens of packages on Friday.
highlights.detail: Updates span AlmaLinux, Debian, Fedora, Gentoo, Mageia, and Oracle, addressing components like bind9, Java, kernel, and graphics libraries. No specific CVE counts are given, but the breadth suggests a coordinated patch cycle.

highlights.title: Beyls: Wrapping up LLVM's relicensing effort
highlights.summary: LLVM’s eight‑year relicensing campaign concludes with over 99.5% of its code now under Apache‑2.0 with the LLVM exception.
highlights.detail: The effort began in 2018 to obtain permissions for code originally under UIUC/NCSA and MIT licenses. Contributions after Jan 19 2019 were automatically under the new license. The remaining uncaptured code is negligible or no longer in the repo.

highlights.title: Vim Classic 8.3.1 released
highlights.summary: Vim Classic 8.3.1 LTS fork is released, incorporating patches up to Vim 8.2.3237 and dropping Python 2 support.
highlights.detail: The release bundles numerous bug fixes, minor features, and plugin compatibility tweaks. It continues the fork’s policy of avoiding large‑language‑model assistance. Full changelog is hosted on sourcehut.

items.summary: The inworld/voice-isolator model on Hugging Face, designed for audio‑to‑audio processing, has 513 likes.

items.title: [$] Bringing the Agama installer to openSUSE Tumbleweed
items.summary: The openSUSE project will adopt the Agama installer as the default for Tumbleweed, after four years of development and its use in Leap 16.0 (2025).
items.detail: Agama has already become the standard installer for openSUSE Leap 16.0 and other flavors. The shift to Tumbleweed raises community concerns about losing some YaST legacy features and RAM requirements for installation.

items.title: Decapitation Seems Like a Great Way to Start X-Mas Decorating
items.summary: A Hackaday piece humorously proposes decapitation as a novel way to start Christmas decorating.
items.detail: The article plays on cultural references, contrasting the familiar Frosty the Snowman story with an absurd DIY suggestion, without providing technical details or instructions.

items.title: HDMI to CSI For Anyone
items.summary: Hackaday outlines a method to convert HDMI output into a CSI camera interface for easier digitization of video streams.
items.detail: While standard HDMI capture devices can be costly or limited, the described approach repurposes a CSI‑compatible board to accept HDMI signals, offering a potentially cheaper and more flexible solution for embedded projects.

items.title: agentscope-ai/agentscope
items.summary: agentscope is a Python library that lets developers build, run, and visualize trustworthy AI agents.
items.detail: The package focuses on transparency and interpretability, providing tools to monitor agent behavior and integrate with existing Python ecosystems. It is hosted on GitHub and gaining traction among AI developers.

items.title: apache/airflow
items.summary: Apache Airflow is an open-source Python platform for authoring, scheduling, and monitoring data workflows.
items.detail: It enables users to define DAGs programmatically, supports extensible operators, and integrates with many services. Airflow is widely adopted for ETL pipelines and data engineering tasks.

items.title: carla-simulator/carla
items.summary: CARLA is an open-source C++ simulator designed for autonomous driving research.
items.detail: The simulator provides realistic urban environments, sensor suites, and physics, allowing researchers to test perception and control algorithms without real vehicles. It supports ROS integration and customizable scenarios.

items.title: elementalsouls/Claude-BugHunter
items.summary: Claude-BugHunter bundles 82 Claude skills, 15 slash commands, and 681 curated vulnerability patterns for bug hunting and red‑team work.
items.detail: The collection covers 24 core vulnerability classes and includes enterprise identity and infrastructure attack matrices. It aims to streamline automated security testing within Claude's code assistant.

items.title: firecrawl/firecrawl
items.summary: Firecrawl offers a single API that searches, scrapes, and accesses data from over 550 providers to enhance AI agents.
items.detail: The service abstracts crawling logic, providing structured outputs for downstream models. It targets developers building knowledge‑base agents that need diverse web content without custom scrapers.

items.title: hypery11/flipper-tesla-fsd
items.summary: Flipper‑Tesla‑FSD is a C++ firmware for Flipper Zero and ESP32 that unlocks Tesla features like FSD region, track mode, and CAN capture via OBD‑II.
items.detail: The project adds functions such as nag killer, blind‑spot alerts, and high‑beam strobe, interfacing through the vehicle's OBD‑II or X179 connector. It expands Flipper Zero's utility for Tesla owners.
